title: AWS Step Functions
description: Build resilient workflows with Step Functions using state machines, parallel and sequential execution, error handling, and the Map state.

data.text: AWS Step Functions is a serverless orchestration service that lets you combine Lambda functions and other AWS services into business-critical applications. You define workflows as state machines using Amazon States Language (ASL).

A Step Functions workflow is a state machine. Each state performs a specific task, such as invoking a Lambda function, making an API call, or waiting. States transition from one to the next based on conditions defined in the workflow.

data.title: Common State Types
items: **Task** — invokes a Lambda function or makes an AWS service call
**Parallel** — runs multiple branches at the same time
**Map** — runs a set of steps for each item in an array
**Wait** — pauses execution for a specified duration
**Succeed / Fail** — ends the execution successfully or with an error

data.text: Sequential workflows run one state after another. Parallel workflows run multiple branches at the same time and wait for all of them to complete. The Map state iterates over an array, running a sub-workflow for each element — useful for processing batches of data.

Step Functions provides built-in error handling with retries and catch blocks. You can specify how many times to retry a failed task and what to do if retries are exhausted. Callbacks let you pause a workflow and resume it when an external process signals completion, which is useful for human approval or long-running jobs.

data.caption: A Step Functions state machine for processing an e-commerce order.
data.definition:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> ValidateOrder
    ValidateOrder --> ProcessPayment: success
    ValidateOrder --> Failed: failed
    ProcessPayment --> ReserveInventory: success
    ProcessPayment --> Failed: payment rejected
    ReserveInventory --> ShipOrder: success
    ReserveInventory --> Failed: out of stock
    ShipOrder --> Success: delivered
    ShipOrder --> Failed: shipping error
    Failed --> [*]
    Success --> [*]

data.title: Why Use Step Functions?
data.text: Step Functions automatically tracks the state of your workflow, retries failed steps, and logs every transition. This means you do not need custom code for retries, timeouts, or status tracking.

terms.definition: A workflow model where the execution moves through defined states in a predictable order.
A state that performs work by invoking a Lambda function or making an AWS API call.
A state that runs multiple branches concurrently and waits for all to complete.
A state that iterates over an array, executing a sub-workflow for each element.
A mechanism to pause execution and resume it later when an external process signals completion.

data.title: Build an Order Processing Workflow
data.description: Create a Step Functions state machine that validates an order, processes payment, reserves inventory, and ships the order.
steps: Design the workflow states in the Step Functions console
Add Lambda tasks for validate, payment, inventory, and shipping
Add Choice states for success and failure paths
Enable retry and catch for the payment step
Start an execution and observe the visual workflow
data.expectedOutcome: A working state machine that successfully processes orders and handles failures gracefully.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Step Functions orchestrates Lambda and other AWS services into reliable workflows
Parallel and Map states enable concurrent and batch processing
Built-in error handling, retries, and callbacks reduce custom code
The visual workflow graph makes debugging and monitoring easy
data.takeaway: Step Functions turns complex, multi-step processes into reliable, observable, and maintainable serverless workflows.
